12.beyond_school: The electronic weighing scale in a shop works on this bridge idea: tiny strain-gauge sensors are arranged as a Wheatstone bridge, and the weight on the pan unbalances it, which the scale turns into a reading.
12.picture: A 16-year-old school girl buying tomatoes at a small Tamil Nadu vegetable shop. The shopkeeper places the tomatoes on a flat electronic weighing scale on the counter. The scale is the large, clear focus, seen close up. Plain shop background, daylight, no brand on the scale.

16.picture: A 16-year-old school boy at home ironing his own white school shirt on an ironing board with an ordinary dry electric iron. The iron is the large, clear focus, seen close up, its cord running to a wall socket. Plain light wall, daylight. No steam, nothing glowing.

1.picture: A 16-year-old school boy sitting at his study table at home, holding an unplugged white phone charger block in his hand and turning it to read the small printed rating on its side. The charger is the large, clear focus, seen close up. His phone and the USB cable rest on the table. Plain wall, daylight. No brand name or logo.

4.picture: A 16-year-old school boy wearing slippers, ironing his white school shirt on an ironing board at home. The iron is plugged into a long orange extension cord that runs across a dry floor; the coiled extension cord is the large, clear focus in the foreground, with the boy and the iron behind it. Nobody touches the cord or the socket. Plain wall, daylight.

11.picture: A simple road junction seen from directly above, like a map: three plain grey roads meet at one point, with only five or six small cars and two-wheelers, some driving in and some driving out. Plain green ground between the roads, no buildings, trees, poles or signboards. Clean, simple and uncluttered, clear daylight.

17.picture: A brick pottery kiln at a small Tamil Nadu pottery unit. A long metal temperature probe is inserted into the side of the kiln, its cable running to a small temperature display on a nearby wall. A potter and a 16-year-old school student look at the display from a safe distance. No open flames in view, plain daylight, simple background.
